title_en: Sinopec Sales Co., Ltd., Shanghai Petroleum Branch, Luojing Oil Depot v. Guangdong Renke Shipping Co., Ltd. — dispute over liability for damage caused by vessel striking
ruling_gist_en: The provisions of Article 17 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Trial of Cases Involving Disputes Related to Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims only cover claims for expenses for the removal, salvage, or clearance of sunken, wrecked, grounded, or abandoned ships and cargo on board, as well as related recourse arising from collisions between ships, but do not cover claims for expenses for the removal or clearance of other submerged objects such as wharf debris, or related recourse arising from a ship striking a wharf or other facilities. Where, in a liability accident involving a ship striking a wharf, recourse is sought against the ship for the costs of removing obstacles within a time limit at the wharf, requiring the shipowner to assume liability for damages from the striking, Article 207, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China shall apply, and such claim shall be recognized as a limitable maritime claim.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over liability for damage caused by ship striking wharf; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Shanghai Municipality; Guangdong Province; legal person; Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China; Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Trial of Cases Involving Disputes Related to Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims; whether wharf clearance costs constitute a limitable maritime claim; determination of liability for ship striking wharf; amended judgment; ship striking wharf; clearance of wharf debris; limitation of liability for maritime claims; application for retrial; dispute over liability for damage caused by a company's ship striking wharf
full_text_en:
Sinopec Sales Co., Ltd. Shanghai Petroleum Branch Luojing Oil Depot v. Guangdong Renke Shipping Co., Ltd. — dispute over vessel berth collision damage liability

Ruling Summary

The provisions of Article 17 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Relating to the Trial of Cases Concerning Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims only apply to claims for the removal and salvage of sunken, wrecked, grounded, or abandoned ships and their cargo, and to related recourse claims arising from collisions between ships. They do not cover claims for the removal and salvage of other submerged objects, such as dock debris, or related recourse claims arising from a vessel's collision with a dock or other facilities. In a liability accident involving a vessel's collision with a dock, recourse claims against the vessel for the costs of clearing the dock within a specified period, and claims for compensation for collision damages against the shipowner, shall be governed by Article 207, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, and shall be recognized as limitation maritime claims.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2014) Min Ti Zi No. 191

Reconsideration Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Guangdong Renke Shipping Co., Ltd. Domicile: Inside the Guangdong Yinzhouhu Paper Industry Base, Shuangshui Town, Xinhui District, Jiangmen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Liang Chaohua, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Chen Zhensheng, lawyer at Shanghai Pacific Ocean Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lin Zhenghui, lawyer at Shanghai Pacific Ocean Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Sinopec Sales Co., Ltd. Shanghai Petroleum Branch Luojing Oil Depot. Domicile: Huangyao Bay, Shengqiao Town, Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Person in Charge: Liang Wei, Manager of the Oil Depot.

Agent ad litem: Chen Youmu, lawyer at Shanghai Yingtai Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yunxin, lawyer at Shanghai Yingtai Law Firm.

In the case concerning the dispute over vessel berth collision damage liability between the Reconsideration Applicant Guangdong Renke Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Renke Company) and the Respondent Sinopec Sales Co., Ltd. Shanghai Petroleum Branch Luojing Oil Depot (formerly Sinopec Shanghai Petroleum Company Limited Shanghai Petroleum Branch Luojing Oil Depot, hereinafter referred to as Luojing Oil Depot), the Shanghai High People's Court rendered a civil judgment on July 17, 2013, (2012) Hu Gao Min Si (Hai) Zhong Zi No. 165. Dissatisfied with the judgment, Renke Company filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court issued a civil ruling on June 27, 2014, (2014) Min Shen Zi No. 668, granting the retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and conducted a public hearing of the case on December 4, 2014. Lin Zhenghui, agent ad litem for Renke Company, and Chen Youmu and Zhang Yunxin, agents ad litem for Luojing Oil Depot, appeared in court for the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

Luojing Oil Depot filed a lawsuit before the Shanghai Maritime Court on March 8, 2011, alleging: On February 3, 2011, the vessel "Renke 1," owned by Renke Company, collided with the Luojing Oil Depot pier due to improper navigation, causing severe damage to the pier and its facilities, as well as casualties among the duty personnel. This resulted in pier repair costs of RMB 17,821,200 (all currency involved in this judgment is in RMB unless otherwise specified as foreign currency), costs for the purchase, transportation, and installation of loading arms of EUR 734,150 (equivalent to RMB 6,284,324), costs for removing obstacles from the damaged pier of RMB 5,600,000, costs for guarding the accident site and the navigation channel of RMB 2,500,000, costs for setting navigational marks of RMB 650,000, maintenance costs during the pier's non-operation period of RMB 7,424,600, loss of property inside the collapsed office building of RMB 30,000, advance payment for personal injury aftermath costs of RMB 44,367.99, and costs for purchasing a temporary duty room of RMB 217,940.09. Therefore, Luojing Oil Depot requested a judgment ordering Renke Company to compensate for the above losses totaling RMB 40,572,432.08, plus interest (calculated from the date of the accident at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period until the date the judgment becomes effective), and to bear the case acceptance fee of RMB 249,948, the pre-litigation preservation application fee of RMB 5,000, and the evidence preservation application fee of RMB 30.

Renke Company argued in its defense that the Luojing Oil Depot pier lacked sufficient lighting and warning signs, and therefore Renke Company should not bear full liability for the accident; that the losses claimed by Luojing Oil Depot were not true; and that all of Luojing Oil Depot's claims were maritime claims for which the responsible party could limit liability under Chapter XI of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as "limitation maritime claims"), and thus Renke Company could lawfully limit its liability.

The first instance trial by the Shanghai Maritime Court found the following facts: On January 31, 2011, the vessel "Renke 1" departed from Qinhuangdao carrying 34,383 tons of coal, planning to berth at No. 3 berth of the Luojing Coal Pier in Shanghai Port at 0200 hours on February 3. After leaving Qinhuangdao, the captain requested a pilot from Renke Company by phone. The company then entrusted the Fujian Provincial Office in Shanghai Shipping Operations Department to arrange pilotage for the vessel. The operations department contacted Shen Yongtao to board the vessel as a pilot. At around 1240 hours on February 2, the "Renke 1" arrived at the Yangtze River estuary anchorage. At around 1900 hours on February 2, the "Renke 1" weighed anchor and resumed navigation. During the voyage, the captain communicated with Shen Yongtao, the pier, tugboats, and others, deciding to advance the berthing plan to 0100 hours on February 3. At around 0006 hours on February 3, Shen Yongtao boarded the "Renke 1." When he boarded, he was not carrying the latest chart data for that section of the waterway or other navigational aids. Captain Chen Xueyuan of the "Renke 1" did not verify Shen Yongtao's pilot qualifications. At around 0010 hours, after learning about the vessel's basic maneuvering characteristics and cargo load, Shen Yongtao began maneuvering the vessel. Subsequently, the "Renke 1" entered the Baoshan Inbound Channel and proceeded upstream at a heading of approximately 300 degrees and a speed of approximately 11 knots. At around 0039 hours, Shen Yongtao misidentified the No. 74 light buoy, and the "Renke 1" mistakenly entered the Baoshan North Channel. At around 0137 hours, it turned around and returned to the Baoshan South Channel, preparing to berth at the Luojing Coal Pier No. 3 berth during the flood tide. Subsequently, the tide was at the end of the flood, with a velocity of 1.5 knots. At around 0152 hours, the "Renke 1" was on a heading of about 286 degrees at a speed of about 9.4 knots, and its position was 400 meters downstream of the north end of Luojing Oil Depot pier, posing a risk of collision. Shen Yongtao ordered a stop and engaged "astern three" gear, but due to the speed of the "Renke 1," the tugboats could not push effectively. At around 0154 hours, the captain immediately put the engine telegraph to full astern and ordered the chief officer to drop anchor. At around 0155 hours, the "Renke 1," at a speed of about 5 knots and a bow direction of 208.3 degrees, collided with the north end of the Luojing Oil Depot pier at an angle of approximately 86 degrees. The accident caused about 74 meters of the eastern section of the north end of the Luojing Oil Depot pier to be destroyed and collapse into the riverbed. The office building built on the pier was also destroyed, causing one death and one injury among the two duty personnel inside, and three loading arms installed on the pier fell into the water and were damaged.

The "Renke 1" is a steel bulk carrier with a gross tonnage of 22,417, engaged in domestic coastal transportation. The registered owner of the vessel is Renke Company. Shen Yongtao, male, born on March 4, 1966, held a Class A First-Class Captain's Competency Certificate issued by Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration on December 12, 2006, and a Certificate of Qualification for Navigating Inland River Routes for Seagoing Vessels (Shanghai to Nanjing) issued by Jiangsu Maritime Safety Administration on March 28, 2008. He did not hold a pilot's competency certificate. The Luojing Oil Depot pier was built in 1993 and largely took shape in 1995. It had not yet been put into operation before the first instance judgment. The pier is F-shaped, capable of berthing 25,000-ton vessels, with a total berth length of 273 meters and a width of 24 meters. An office building was constructed at each of the north and south ends. Nighttime lighting at the pier relied on searchlights on the office buildings and warning lights at both ends of the pier. At the time of the accident, the pier's searchlights and warning lights were all functioning normally.

On March 4, 2011, the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration issued the "Investigation Report on the '2.3' 'Renke 1' Vessel Collision with the Shanghai Port Luojing Oil Depot Pier Accident," concluding that the accident was a single-party liability accident in which the "Renke 1" struck a fixed pier during navigation. After the accident, to ensure the safety of navigable waters and prevent secondary accidents, the Shanghai Baoshan Maritime Safety Office took safety protection measures at the accident site waters, set up special buoys, commissioned Shanghai Pujiang Salvage and Dredging Engineering Co., Ltd. to conduct underwater surveys near the damaged pier, and dispatched vessels to guard the accident site. This generated costs for guarding the accident site and the navigation channel and costs for setting navigational marks. On June 16, 2011, the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration issued an "Administrative Compulsory Measures Decision" to Luojing Oil Depot, requiring Luojing Oil Depot to remove and salvage the pier debris affecting the navigation channel within a specified period. Luojing Oil Depot then signed a contract with Shanghai Darun Salvage Engineering Co., Ltd., commissioning it to remove the debris, thus incurring obstacle removal costs.

During the first instance trial, Luojing Oil Depot and Renke Company jointly selected Shanghai Zhongjiu Engineering Testing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongjiu Company) and the Ninth Design and Research Institute Engineering Co., Ltd., China State Shipbuilding Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Zhongjiu Research Institute) as appraisal and evaluation institutions to appraise and evaluate the accident and the damage to the pier. Zhongjiu Company issued the "Comprehensive Inspection Report on the '2011.2.3' Damage Accident of the 25,000-ton Oil Pier of Sinopec Shanghai Petroleum Branch Luojing Oil Depot," and Zhongjiu Research Institute issued the "Design for the Repair Plan for the Marine Damage to the 25,000-ton Oil Pier of Sinopec Shanghai Petroleum Branch Luojing Oil Depot." The appraisal and evaluation conclusion was that the cost to repair the damaged pier was RMB 16,227,800. Luojing Oil Depot and Renke Company jointly commissioned Shanghai Shuangxi Marine Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shuangxi Company) to appraise and evaluate the damage to the loading arms. Shuangxi Company issued an inspection report, concluding that the cost to repair the damaged loading arms was RMB 2,000,000. During the court hearing in the first instance, Luojing Oil Depot and Renke Company confirmed that the costs for removing debris from the damaged pier were RMB 5,600,000; the costs for guarding the accident site and the navigation channel were RMB 2,500,000 (of which RMB 2,000,000 had been paid by Renke Company); the costs for setting navigational marks were RMB 650,000; and the loss of property inside the collapsed office building was RMB 30,000. Additionally, both Luojing Oil Depot and Renke Company confirmed that the appraisal and evaluation conclusions of Zhongjiu Company and Zhongjiu Research Institute would be the final basis for determining the cost of repairing the damaged pier, and that the appraisal and evaluation conclusion of Shuangxi Company would be the final basis for determining the cost of repairing the damaged loading arms. Furthermore, due to the destruction of the office building on the pier, Luojing Oil Depot purchased container-type mobile homes from Shanghai Kuaijie Mobile House Co., Ltd. for use as temporary duty rooms, actually paying RMB 211,567.09.

On February 22, 2011, Renke Company applied to the Shanghai Maritime Court to establish a limitation fund for maritime claims. The court granted the application on May 3, 2011, by civil ruling (2011) Hu Hai Fa Xian Zi No. 1, setting the fund amount at 1,913,569.50 Special Drawing Rights (converted into RMB 19,805,444.33 at the exchange rate on the date the ruling became effective, May 19, 2011) plus interest of RMB 362,093.03 (calculated from the date of the accident, February 3, 2011, to the date the fund was established, May 20, 2011, at the benchmark one-year lending rate of financial institutions determined by the People's Bank of China for the same period), totaling RMB 20,167,537.36. On May 20, 2011, Renke Company submitted to the Shanghai Maritime Court a guarantee letter from Guangdong Branch of BOC Insurance Co., Ltd., guaranteeing the establishment of the limitation fund for maritime claims.

The Shanghai Maritime Court held in the first instance: The location of the Luojing Oil Depot pier was printed on the nautical charts, and its lighting facilities and warning signs complied with relevant regulations. The cause of the collision was that the "Renke 1," while being navigated by a person without pilot qualifications, deviated from the correct channel, did not use a safe speed to meet the berthing time, and was improperly maneuvered while berthing. Therefore, Renke Company should bear full responsibility. Based on the agreement voluntarily reached by the parties, the conclusions of the appraisal and evaluation institutions jointly selected by the parties, the valid evidence in the case, and considering the relevance and reasonableness of the losses, the court determined Luojing Oil Depot's losses as follows: repair costs for the damaged pier of RMB 16,227,800; repair costs for the damaged loading arms of RMB 2,000,000; obstacle removal costs for the damaged pier of RMB 5,600,000; accident site and navigation channel guarding costs of RMB 500,000 (after deducting the RMB 2,000,000 already paid by Renke Company); costs for setting navigational marks of RMB 650,000; loss of property inside the collapsed office building of RMB 30,000; and costs for purchasing a temporary duty room of RMB 211,567.09. Given that the above costs were all expenses incurred by Luojing Oil Depot, interest on the loss should be calculated from the date the expenses were incurred. Since Luojing Oil Depot provided evidence of actual payment only for the temporary duty room purchase cost of RMB 211,567.09, interest could be calculated from the date of the last payment for this item (October 13, 2011) to the date the judgment became effective, at the demand deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period. There was no evidence in this case that the accident was caused by Renke Company's intention or reckless act or omission with knowledge that damage would probably result. Therefore, Renke Company should not lose the right to limit its liability for maritime claims. The provisions of Article 17, Paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Relating to the Trial of Cases Concerning Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims, concerning recourse for refloating, clearing, etc., do not apply to vessel collision accidents involving only one party's liability. The term "responsible party" in that clause should be understood as the subject liable for compensation in a maritime accident, i.e., the person responsible for the accident. Since the owner of the Luojing Oil Depot pier did not bear liability for the accident in the vessel collision, its recourse against the offending vessel for losses such as clearance costs should not be subject to the vessel's limitation of liability. This reflects the protection of the rights of the non-negligent party and also the protection of the rights of owners of shipping facilities such as docks and navigation channels, which is conducive to ensuring navigation convenience and safety in ports. The costs incurred by Luojing Oil Depot for the refloating, removal, destruction, or rendering harmless of the debris from the damaged pier, including the obstacle removal costs for the damaged pier, the accident site and navigation channel guarding costs, and the costs for setting navigational marks, are all non-limitation maritime claims. The repair costs for the damaged pier, repair costs for the damaged loading arms, loss of property inside the collapsed office building, and costs for purchasing the temporary duty room and their interest are limitation maritime claims. Since the total amount of limitation maritime claims does not exceed the amount of the fund and its interest during the establishment period, Renke Company should compensate Luojing Oil Depot for all losses. In summary, in accordance with Article 6, Paragraph 1 and Article 15 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 204, 207, Paragraph 1, Item 1, and Article 209 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China; Article 4 and Article 9 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Relating to the Trial of Vessel Collision Dispute Cases; Articles 17, 18, and 19 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Relating to the Trial of Cases Concerning Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims; Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Compensation for Property Damage in Vessel Collision and Contact Cases; and Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2007 Amendment), the Shanghai Maritime Court rendered a civil judgment on September 21, 2012, (2011) Hu Hai Fa Hai Chu Zi No. 17: (1) Renke Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Luojing Oil Depot for the repair costs of the damaged pier of RMB 16,227,800, repair costs of the damaged loading arms of RMB 2,000,000, obstacle removal costs of the damaged pier of RMB 5,600,000, accident site and navigation channel guarding costs of RMB 500,000, costs for setting navigational marks of RMB 650,000, loss of property inside the collapsed office building of RMB 30,000, and costs for purchasing the temporary duty room of RMB 211,567.09, totaling RMB 25,219,367.09; (2) Renke Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Luojing Oil Depot for the interest loss on the costs for purchasing the temporary duty room of RMB 211,567.09 (calculated from October 13, 2011, to the effective date of this judgment at the demand deposit interest rate determined by the People's Bank of China for the same period); (3) The other claims of Luojing Oil Depot are dismissed. If Renke Company fails to perform the obligation to pay money within the period specified in this judgment, it shall pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2007 Amendment). The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 249,948 shall be borne by Luojing Oil Depot in the amount of RMB 98,528.60 and by Renke Company in the amount of RMB 151,419.40; the pre-litigation preservation application fee of RMB 5,000 and the evidence preservation application fee of RMB 30 shall be borne by Renke Company.

Renke Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court.

Renke Company argued on appeal: (1) The first instance judgment was erroneous in determining the amount of damages Renke Company should compensate Luojing Oil Depot. The pier in question had never been put into operation before the accident, and equating the loss costs to the cost of rebuilding a qualified pier was unreasonable. Even if the pier were considered a qualified pier, depreciation for the years it had been in use should have been deducted when assessing the loss. The costs for guarding the accident site and navigation channel and for setting navigational marks were incurred because Luojing Oil Depot failed to actively perform its duty to mitigate losses. Luojing Oil Depot's claim for the cost of purchasing a temporary duty room constituted a duplicate claim. (2) The first instance judgment erred in law by classifying the claims for obstacle removal costs of the damaged pier, accident site and navigation channel guarding costs, and costs for setting navigational marks as non-limitation maritime claims. The provisions of Article 17 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Relating to the Trial of Cases Concerning Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims apply only to vessel collision cases, but this case, involving vessel contact, could also be applied by reference. The claims for these costs should be limitation maritime claims. The first instance judgment found some facts unclearly and applied the law incorrectly. Accordingly, Renke Company requested that the appellate court set aside items (1) and (2) of the first instance judgment, and instead enter a judgment ordering Renke Company to compensate Luojing Oil Depot for losses of RMB 5,630,000 (including RMB 2,000,000 for repair costs of the damaged loading arms, RMB 5,600,000 for obstacle removal costs of the damaged pier, and RMB 30,000 for loss of property inside the collapsed office building, after deducting RMB 2,000,000 already advanced by Renke Company on behalf of Luojing Oil Depot); and also hold that Luojing Oil Depot's claims for obstacle removal costs of the pier, accident site and navigation channel guarding costs, and costs for setting navigational marks are limitation maritime claims.

Luo Jing Oil Depot argued in its defense: (1) The amount of losses that the first instance judgment found Renke Company should compensate Luo Jing Oil Depot was correctly determined. The findings of the expert appraisal regarding the actual damage to the dock and the repair costs were jointly accepted by both Luo Jing Oil Depot and Renke Company, and the first instance judgment's determination of losses based on this was not improper; the costs for guarding the accident site and the navigation channel, as well as the costs for setting up navigation marks, were reasonable expenses incurred to prevent secondary accidents and fall within the scope of damages in this case; the cost of purchasing a temporary duty room for the dock was an actual separate loss and not a duplicate claim. (2) The first instance judgment's classification of the claims for the costs of clearing obstacles from the damaged dock, guarding the accident site and navigation channel, and setting up navigation marks as non-limitable maritime claims was in accordance with the law. Claims for the costs of clearing and salvaging sunken vessels and objects are not among the limitable maritime claims listed in Article 207(1) of the Maritime Code of the PRC. Furthermore, Article 17 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Related to the Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims specifies that claims for the costs of clearing and salvaging obstacles are non-limitable maritime claims, with only one exception (where, in a ship collision case, the owner of the sunken ship recovers the costs of clearing and salvaging obstacles from the other responsible party for the accident), which falls within the scope of limitation of liability for maritime claims. The accident in this case, involving a ship striking a dock, does not fall within the aforementioned exception. The first instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Accordingly, Luo Jing Oil Depot requested that the appellate court dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

During the second instance, neither party submitted new evidence. The Shanghai High People's Court, upon trial in the second instance, found that the facts ascertained by the Shanghai Maritime Court in the first instance were substantially true.

The Shanghai High People's Court held in the second instance: This case is a dispute over liability for damage caused by a ship striking a dock. Luo Jing Oil Depot suffered losses due to the striking accident. During the first instance, after consultation, Luo Jing Oil Depot and Renke Company jointly selected and commissioned Zhongjiu Company and Zhongjiu Research Institute as expert appraisal agencies to appraise and evaluate the accident and the damage to the dock. The appraisal procedures were lawful, and the appraisal conclusions were confirmed by both parties during the first instance. The first instance court's determination of the repair costs for the damaged dock based on these appraisal conclusions was not improper. The costs for guarding the accident site and navigation channel and for setting up navigation marks were incurred for public safety and the public interest, not due to Luo Jing Oil Depot's failure to fulfill its duty to mitigate losses. Luo Jing Oil Depot's claim for the purchase of a temporary duty room for the dock was to replace the function of the dock's comprehensive building that was destroyed in the accident, and the function of the destroyed comprehensive building could not be replaced by the part of the comprehensive building on the undamaged section of the dock. Renke Company's assertion that the first instance judgment erroneously determined Luo Jing Oil Depot's losses lacked factual basis. Claims for the costs of clearing and salvaging the sunken ship and objects arising from the striking accident do not fall within the limitable maritime claims specified in Chapter 11 of the Maritime Code of the PRC. Renke Company's grounds for appeal were untenable. Accordingly, on July 17, 2013, the Shanghai High People's Court issued Civil Judgment (2012) Hu Gao Min Si (Hai) Zhong Zi No. 165, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 151,419.40 was to be borne by Renke Company.

Renke Company, dissatisfied with both the first and second instance judgments, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: (1) The first and second instance judgments erroneously determined the amount of losses to Luo Jing Oil Depot's dock. Luo Jing Oil Depot could not prove that its dock was a legally compliant facility; the dock in question should be deemed an unauthorized construction that could not actually be put into operation. The value of the dock should be the residual value of its component parts minus the cost of demolition. The first and second instance judgments determined the value of the damage based on the cost of rebuilding a compliant dock project without deducting depreciation, which was baseless. The dock in question had another comprehensive building that could meet duty needs, and Luo Jing Oil Depot's claim against Renke Company for the cost of purchasing a temporary duty room, in addition to claiming dock repair costs, was clearly a duplicate claim. The location of the wreckage of the damaged dock was within the waters managed and operated by Luo Jing Oil Depot itself, not navigable waters, and had nothing to do with the normal navigation of any vessel or the public interest; the cost of salvaging the dock wreckage was not actually a cost of clearing obstacles. The majority of the costs for guarding the accident site and navigation channel and setting up navigation marks were incurred because Luo Jing Oil Depot failed to promptly salvage and clear the wreckage and failed to reasonably fulfill its duty to mitigate losses, and thus should not be borne by Renke Company. During the first instance, Luo Jing Oil Depot claimed RMB 2.5 million for guarding the accident site and navigation channel and RMB 650,000 for setting up navigation marks. Renke Company, through court mediation during the first instance, acknowledged the amounts of these two costs but explicitly stated that these costs were not reasonable expenses arising from the striking incident and never acknowledged that these costs should be borne by Renke Company. (2) The first and second instance judgments erroneously applied the law in finding that Renke Company was not entitled to limit its liability for maritime claims regarding the claims for costs of clearing obstacles from the damaged dock, guarding the accident site and navigation channel, and setting up navigation marks. Article 207(1)(1) of the Maritime Code of the PRC clearly stipulates that limitable maritime claims include "claims in respect of damage to port works, basins, waterways, and navigational aids, and for consequential loss arising therefrom." A dock is clearly a type of port work. The "Renke 1" vessel struck the Luo Jing Oil Depot dock while navigating, and the resulting costs of clearing obstacles, guarding, and setting up navigation marks were all losses arising from the striking accident. Renke Company is legally entitled to limit its liability. Article 17 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Related to the Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims only concerns collisions between ships and does not cover situations where a ship strikes a dock, nor does it apply to costs for setting up navigation marks or guarding costs. Given that Renke Company had already compensated RMB 2 million for guarding the accident site and navigation channel in advance, this RMB 2 million should be deducted when determining Renke Company's total compensation amount in this case based on the statutory limitation amount. In summary, the first and second instance judgments found the facts unclearly and applied the law erroneously. Renke Company requested: set aside the second instance judgment; set aside items 1 and 2 of the first instance judgment; amend the judgment to order Renke Company to compensate Luo Jing Oil Depot for losses of RMB 5.63 million; confirm that Renke Company is legally entitled to claim limitation of liability for maritime claims regarding the losses from the costs of clearing obstacles from the damaged dock, guarding the accident site and navigation channel, and setting up navigation marks.

Luo Jing Oil Depot argued in defense: (1) The Luo Jing Oil Depot dock was a fully compliant dock that had passed completion acceptance and obtained approvals and quality recognition from relevant competent authorities. The repair plan for the dock in question was a budget estimate based on repairing the actual damage to the dock, i.e., an appraisal of the cost to restore the dock to its original condition. Both parties during the first instance acknowledged the appraisal conclusions regarding the dock repair plan and costs. The dock in question had not yet been put into operation at the time of the accident, so there was no situation requiring the deduction of depreciation for years of use. The cost of purchasing a temporary duty room for the dock was a necessary replacement cost, and Luo Jing Oil Depot's claim for this compensation did not constitute a duplicate claim. The wreckage of the dock that fell into the navigation channel after being struck was an obstruction to navigation, and the cost of clearing it was a cost of clearing obstacles to ensure public safety. The costs for guarding the accident site and navigation channel and setting up navigation marks were all paid under the orders and requirements of the maritime competent authority and were costs of taking reasonable measures to protect the public interest, and thus should fall within the scope of damages. (2) Renke Company should not be entitled to the right to limit liability for maritime claims. Renke Company employed persons without pilotage qualifications to provide pilotage, directly causing the accident; Renke Company, despite knowing about the latest nautical charts, failed to equip the "Renke 1" vessel with the latest charts and did not install an electronic chart navigation system, rendering the vessel unseaworthy; Renke Company was negligent in the safety management of the vessel, laying hidden dangers for the accident. Renke Company's conduct involved reckless conduct, meeting the conditions under Article 209 of the Maritime Code of the PRC for the responsible party to lose the right to limit liability for maritime claims. (3) The costs of clearing obstacles, guarding, and setting up navigation marks are not limitable maritime claims. The limitable maritime claims specified in Article 207 of the Maritime Code of the PRC do not include claims for costs of clearing obstacles, guarding, and setting up navigation marks. Under current judicial interpretations, costs for clearing and salvaging obstacles involving public safety and the public interest are non-limitable maritime claims with only one exception, namely, in ship collision cases, the opposing party of the sunken ship can enjoy the limitation of liability for maritime claims for the sunken ship's costs of clearing and salvaging obstacles. There are no other exceptions. Luo Jing Oil Depot, after implementing the forced clearing and salvaging according to the requirements of the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration and bearing the corresponding costs, claimed against Renke Company. This claim does not fall within the scope of limitable maritime claims. In summary, Renke Company's application for retrial lacked factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

This Court finds: The facts found by the Shanghai Maritime Court and the Shanghai High People's Court are supported by relevant evidence, and neither party raised objections; this Court confirms them.

During the retrial of this Court, Luo Jing Oil Depot additionally provided the following three pieces of evidence: 1. An article published in the journal "Shanghai Maritime" (Issue 2, 2011), hosted by the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration, entitled "Shanghai Maritime Cracks Down on Illegal Pilotage," intended to prove that the owner of the "Renke 1" vessel tolerated illegal pilotage to ensure the vessel's schedule; 2. Criminal Judgment (2012) Yang Xing Chu Zi No. 59 of the Yangpu District People's Court of Shanghai, intended to prove that the illegal pilotage involved in the case was serious, and Shen Yongtao was sentenced to 4 years' imprisonment by the court for the crime of causing a traffic accident; 3. Information published on the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration website on August 24, 2011, entitled "Shanghai Baoshan Maritime Safety Administration Organizes a Coordination Meeting on the Navigation Safety of Clearing and Salvaging Obstacles at the Luo Jing Oil Depot Dock," intended to prove that the obstacle clearing project at Luo Jing Oil Depot was a measure forced by the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration to protect the public interest and ensure navigation safety.

After examination, Renke Company acknowledged the authenticity of the aforementioned journal and judgment but argued that none of the three pieces of evidence constituted new evidence, were irrelevant to the case, were hearsay evidence containing speculative content, and were insufficient to prove the facts asserted by Luo Jing Oil Depot.

Upon review, the content of evidence 1 is promotional information and is not a formal determination of responsibility by the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration; the "Water Traffic Accident Responsibility Determination Letter" issued by the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration on August 9, 2011, regarding the accident in question did not find that the owner of the "Renke 1" vessel tolerated illegal pilotage, and the content that Luo Jing Oil Depot sought to prove with this evidence lacks corroboration from other evidence, so this Court does not accept it. Evidence 2 does not contain content regarding the degree of fault of Renke Company itself, and the facts it proves do not affect the civil liability for compensation (including the right to limit liability for maritime claims) that Renke Company should bear; this evidence is irrelevant to the dispute in this case and is not adopted by this Court. The relevant information contained in evidence 3 can be corroborated by the "Maritime Administrative Compulsory Measures Decision Letter" issued by the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration to Luo Jing Oil Depot on June 16, 2011, and this Court accepts it.

This Court further finds: The Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration issued a "Maritime Administrative Compulsory Measures Decision Letter" to Luo Jing Oil Depot on June 16, 2011, stating: "The waters of the Luo Jing Oil Depot dock have dense vessel traffic, and the damaged, collapsed, and submerged portion of the dock has seriously affected the navigation safety of these waters." The Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration issued a "Water Traffic Accident Responsibility Determination Letter" on August 9, 2011, regarding the accident in question, which stated the cause of the accident as follows: (1) The "pilot" Shen Yongtao was unfamiliar with the navigation channel, changed the berthing plan at the last moment, failed to use a safe speed, and made serious errors in driving and maneuvering the vessel, which was the direct cause of the accident. (2) The illegal pilotage business conducted by the agency company was one of the causes of the accident. (3) The captain's failure to effectively fulfill his responsibility for vessel safety management was also one of the causes of the accident. The Shanghai Maritime Court accepted Renke Company's application to establish a fund for the limitation of liability for maritime claims regarding the striking accident on February 22, 2011, and published consecutive notices in the People's Court Daily from March 24 to 26, 2011, regarding the acceptance of the application to establish the fund for limiting liability. During the period for applying for registration of claims specified in the notices, only one creditor, Luo Jing Oil Depot, applied to the Shanghai Maritime Court for registration of claims related to the accident.

This Court holds: This case is a dispute over liability for damage caused by a ship striking a dock. Based on Renke Company's application for retrial and Luo Jing Oil Depot's defense, the key issues for the retrial are: (1) Determination of losses from the ship striking; (2) Whether Renke Company is in a situation where it loses the right to limit liability for maritime claims under the law; (3) Whether Renke Company is entitled to claim limitation of liability for the claims for costs of clearing obstacles from the damaged dock, guarding the accident site and navigation channel, and setting up navigation marks.

(1) Regarding the determination of losses from the ship striking

The Luo Jing Oil Depot dock was damaged due to the unilateral fault of the "Renke 1" vessel in the striking accident, and Renke Company should bear full liability for compensation. Regarding the losses from the ship striking accident, both parties jointly selected an expert appraisal agency during the first instance and confirmed that the appraisal conclusions of Zhongjiu Company and Zhongjiu Research Institute would serve as the final basis for determining the repair costs for the damaged dock, and that the appraisal conclusions of Shuangxi Company would serve as the final basis for determining the repair costs for the damaged oil loading arm. The first and second instance judgments' determination of the relevant repair costs based on this was not improper. The dock in question was substantially constructed in 1995 and had not yet been put into operation before the first instance judgment was rendered. The dock is owned and managed by Luo Jing Oil Depot. Although Luo Jing Oil Depot did not provide documentation of the dock's completion acceptance during the litigation, the repair plan for the dock in question was mainly aimed at restoring the dock to its condition before the damage, and did not explicitly propose to repair and rebuild it to the standard of a compliant dock. Regardless of whether the dock had passed completion acceptance before the damage, Renke Company is obligated to restore it to its original condition. Renke Company's denial of its compensation obligation on the grounds that the first and second instance judgments determined the repair costs based on the cost of rebuilding a compliant dock lacks factual basis and is not supported by this Court. Since the dock in question was not put into operation, the first and second instance judgments' failure to deduct depreciation when determining the losses was not improper. After the dock in question was struck by the "Renke 1" vessel, the comprehensive building constructed on the northern end of the dock was also destroyed. This comprehensive building originally had specific purposes, including accommodating duty personnel and providing nighttime lighting for the dock. Given that the dock in question required a certain period of time for repair, Luo Jing Oil Depot's purchase of a container mobile house as a temporary duty room during the repair period incurred costs of RMB 211,567.09, which was a necessary temporary replacement cost. Luo Jing Oil Depot's simultaneous claim for the cost of purchasing the temporary duty room and the dock repair costs does not constitute a duplicate claim. Luo Jing Oil Depot immediately commissioned a salvage operator to clear the dock wreckage based on the administrative decision of the Shanghai Maritime Safety Administration to salvage and clear within a time limit. The resulting costs of clearing obstacles were costs necessarily incurred to ensure the navigability of the channel. There is no evidence in this case that Luo Jing Oil Depot violated its duty to reasonably mitigate losses in clearing the dock wreckage. After the striking accident at the dock in question, to prevent secondary accidents, special buoys were set up in the waters of the accident site and ships were dispatched to guard the accident site, resulting in costs for guarding the accident site and navigation channel and setting up navigation marks. These were costs of necessary measures to ensure the safety of navigation in the waters. The costs of clearing obstacles, guarding the accident site and navigation channel, and setting up navigation marks are all losses suffered by Luo Jing Oil Depot due to the dock being struck, and Renke Company should compensate for them. Renke Company's argument that it should not compensate for these costs lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported by this Court. The first and second instance judgments' determination of the accident losses has sufficient factual and legal basis and is affirmed by this Court.

(2) Regarding whether Renke Company is in a situation where it loses the right to limit liability for maritime claims under the law

The accident in question was caused by the illegal pilotage arranged by the shipping agent commissioned by Renke Company, the negligence of the pilot and the captain and crew in navigating the vessel, and the captain's negligence in safety management of the vessel. There is no evidence in this case that the losses from the accident were caused by Renke Company's intentional conduct or reckless conduct with knowledge that loss would probably result. The first instance judgment's finding that Renke Company should not lose the right to limit liability for maritime claims was not improper. Luo Jing Oil Depot did not appeal this finding after the first instance judgment. Its argument in the retrial defense that Renke Company should not enjoy the right to limit liability for maritime claims, without providing evidence and reasons sufficient to overturn the relevant finding of the first instance judgment, is not supported by this Court.

(3) Regarding whether Renke Company is entitled to claim limitation of liability for the claims for costs of clearing obstacles from the damaged dock, guarding the accident site and navigation channel, and setting up navigation marks

Article 207 of the Maritime Code of the PRC provides for limitable maritime claims, with Article 207(1)(1) stating: "Claims in respect of loss of life or personal injury or loss of or damage to property occurring on board a ship or directly in connection with the operation of the ship or with salvage operations, including claims in respect of damage to port works, basins, waterways and navigational aids, and for consequential loss arising therefrom." The "Renke 1" vessel struck the Luo Jing Oil Depot dock, resulting in losses including dock repair costs, oil loading arm repair costs, losses of property inside the collapsed comprehensive building, the cost of purchasing a temporary duty room for the dock and interest, costs for guarding the accident site and navigation channel, and costs for setting up navigation marks. Claims for these losses fall within the limitable maritime claims provided for in the aforementioned legal provision. In accordance with the legislative intent of Article 207(1) of the Maritime Code of the PRC, Article 17(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Related to the Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims stipulates: "The maritime claims for which liability may be limited under Article 207 of the Maritime Code shall not include claims arising from the refloating, removal, destruction, or rendering harmless of a ship that is sunk, wrecked, stranded, or abandoned, or claims arising from the removal, destruction, or rendering harmless of cargo on board such a ship." Furthermore, Article 17(2) of the same Provisions stipulates: "Where a person liable incurs a claim as specified in the preceding paragraph due to a collision between ships, and the person liable seeks recourse from the opposing ship for the losses thus incurred, if the person against whom the claim is made asserts the right to limit liability in accordance with Article 207 of the Maritime Code, such assertion shall be supported." The provisions of this Article only concern claims for the costs of refloating, removing, destroying, or rendering harmless sunken, wrecked, stranded, or abandoned ships and cargo on board, and related recourse arising from collisions between ships. In a liability accident where a ship strikes a dock, a claim for recourse against the ship for the costs of clearing obstacles from the dock within a time limit, requiring the shipowner to bear liability for damage caused by the striking, should be governed by Article 207(1)(1) of the Maritime Code of the PRC and be determined as a limitable maritime claim. The first and second instance judgments' determination that the costs of clearing obstacles from the damaged dock, guarding the accident site and navigation channel, and setting up navigation marks are non-limitable maritime claims does not comply with the law. Renke Company's application for retrial on this ground is justified and should be supported.

RENKE Company has the right to claim limitation of liability for maritime claims with respect to all damages claims by Luojing Oil Depot arising from the berth collision. All damages claims of Luojing Oil Depot (including the RMB 2,000,000 in accident site and waterway watch-keeping fees already paid by RENKE Company) shall be satisfied within the scope of the fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims established by RENKE Company in the amount of RMB 20,167,537.36 and the interest accrued thereon during the period of the fund's establishment (calculated at the one-year benchmark lending rate for financial institutions as determined by the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period). Luojing Oil Depot is the sole creditor that has registered a claim. RENKE Company has already compensated RMB 2,000,000 for the accident site and waterway watch-keeping fees. Therefore, RENKE Company's liability for damages in this case shall be reduced accordingly. The damages claims of Luojing Oil Depot as affirmed by this Judgment shall be satisfied within the scope of the balance of RMB 18,167,537.36 after deducting RMB 2,000,000 from the aforementioned fund and the interest accrued during the period of the fund's establishment.

In summary, the facts found in the first-instance and second-instance judgments were clear, but the application of law was partially erroneous, and this Court hereby corrects the same. Pursuant to Article 207, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 207, paragraph 1, and Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (No. 165, [2012] Shanghai High People's Court, Civil Division IV (Maritime), Final) of the Shanghai High People's Court is reversed.

2. Items 1 and 2 of the civil judgment (No. 17, [2011] Shanghai Maritime Court, Civil Division (Maritime), First Instance) of the Shanghai Maritime Court are affirmed.

3. Item 3 of the civil judgment (No. 17, [2011] Shanghai Maritime Court, Civil Division (Maritime), First Instance) of the Shanghai Maritime Court is amended to: The above damages shall be satisfied within the balance of RMB 18,167,537.36 after deducting the compensation amount already paid by RENKE Company from the fund for limitation of liability for maritime claims established by RENKE Company, and the interest accrued during the period of establishment of the fund of RMB 20,167,537.36 (calculated at the one-year benchmark lending rate for financial institutions as determined by the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period).

If the monetary obligation is not performed within the period specified in this Judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
